grade.first_issue: In the uniqueness argument, the two transformed inequalities are combined incorrectly. Correct elimination of the terms involving ε(x) gives (x-y)^2+ε(y)^2≥2(x-y)ε(y), namely ((x-y)-ε(y))^2≥0, not the claimed restrictive quadratic.
grade.summary: The claimed classification is false. For every c≥0, f(t)=t+c is admissible: the two original inequalities are exactly RMS–AM and AM–GM applied to x and y+c. Thus f(t)=t+1 is a direct counterexample to the assertion that only f(t)=t works, so Rule A caps the score at 2. The submission earns limited credit for correctly squaring the inequalities and verifying the c=0 solution, but its central uniqueness argument begins with an invalid algebraic inference and cannot be locally repaired into the correct classification.
strengths: Correctly squares and reformulates both inequalities using positivity.
Correctly verifies that f(x)=x is an admissible solution.

errors.description: The final answer omits all valid solutions f(x)=x+c with c>0; for these functions both inequalities follow from the standard RMS–AM–GM inequalities.
The elimination of ε(x) is algebraically invalid. The actual consequence is the tautology ((x-y)-ε(y))^2≥0, so it provides no restriction on ε(y).

Later, the proof passes from the existence of one nonzero ε(y) to an argument assuming f(y)≤y/2 for all y, which was not established. Its subsequent minimization over x is also unjustified because ε(x)=0 was assumed only for a particular x, not for every x over which the minimum is taken.
